title: حِكَايَةُ عَلِيِّ بْنِ بَكَّارٍ مَعَ شَمْسِ النَّهَارِ
titleEn: ʿAlī ibn Bakkār and Shams al-Nahār
part: Night 168 · ʿAlī ibn Bakkār and Shams al-Nahār, continued
source: William Hay Macnaghten, ed., The Alif Laila, or Book of the Thousand Nights and One Night, vol. 1, Calcutta 1839 (“Calcutta II”), printed pp. 805–809 (Night 168, continuing directly from nights-167), transcribed from the 300 ppi scan (archive.org aliflailaorbooko01macn) by the editors' own transcription. The edition prints the prose essentially unpointed: ALL VOCALIZATION (tashkīl) IS EDITORIAL — ours, not the edition's — and the alphabet button strips it back to the bare rasm as Macnaghten prints it, except where a clear misprint has been corrected (each is noted). Romanization is simplified IJMES. Spelling, including the edition’s Middle Arabic forms, is preserved; clear misprints are corrected in the text, and the note on each gives the print’s reading. Obscure or doubtful forms are kept as printed, vocalized by evident sense and flagged in the notes. Read-aloud audio is a Modern Standard Arabic reading of this vocalised text, synthesized by machine, with word-by-word timing generated the same way.
about: Night 168 continues the tale of ʿAlī ibn Bakkār and Shams al-Nahār. The slave-girl urges the jeweller to warn ʿAlī, and he finds him still dreaming of union. ʿAlī flees Baghdad with him in disguise, but on the road robbers kill his servants and strip them of everything. Naked and hungry, they shelter in a town's mosque until a stranger takes them home, clothes and feeds them. That night ʿAlī entrusts the jeweller with his last wishes for his mother; hearing a girl sing verses on parting, he gives a great cry and dies. The jeweller returns to Baghdad and breaks the news to ʿAlī's mother, and on his way home a woman seizes him by the hand. As with every printed edition of the Nights, this one belongs to the late Egyptian recension (ZER) — an eighteenth-century expansion padded out to a literal 1001 nights; no printed edition is a medieval text, and Macnaghten regularised the language here and there, so some Middle Arabic texture is a nineteenth-century retrofit.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا كَانَتِ اللَّيْلَةُ الثَّامِنَةُ وَالسِّتُّونَ بَعْدَ الْمِائَةِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā kānati al-laylatu al-thāminatu wa-al-sittūna baʿda al-miʾati
sentences.l: And when it was the night, the eighth-and-sixty after the hundred,
sentences.i: And when it was the hundred and sixty-eighth night,
sentences.n: The heading is built as before: al-thāmina, “the eighth”, feminine to agree with layla; then wa-al-sittūn, “and the sixty”; then baʿda al-miʾa, “after the hundred”.

sentences.t: قَالَتْ بَلَغَنِي أَيُّهَا الْمَلِكُ السَّعِيدُ أَنَّ الْجَارِيَةَ قَالَتْ لِلْجَوْهَرِيِّ إِنَّ سَيِّدَتِى لَمْ يَكُنْ عِنْدَهَا أَقْرَبُ وَأَحْفَظُ لِكِتْمَانِ السِّرِّ مِنِّي
sentences.tr: qālat balaghanī ayyuhā al-maliku al-saʿīdu anna al-jāriyata qālat li-al-jawhariyyi inna sayyidatī lam yakun ʿindahā aqrabu wa-aḥfaẓu li-kitmāni al-sirri minnī
sentences.l: She-said: It-has-reached-me, O fortunate king, that the slave-girl said to-the-jeweller: (Indeed) my-mistress, there-was-not with-her (one) nearer and better-keeping for the hiding of the secret than-me.
sentences.i: She said: It has reached me, O fortunate king, that the slave-girl said to the jeweller, “My mistress has no one about her better fitted than I am, or more to be trusted, to keep the secret.
sentences.n: The night opens by repeating the girl's last words from the night before, this time in a cleaner form: lam yakun ʿindahā aqrabu wa-aḥfaẓu … minnī, “there was not with her (anyone) nearer and better at keeping … than I”. The elatives aqrabu and aḥfaẓu stand as the subject of yakun, with the person they describe left unsaid; min after an elative is “than”. li-kitmāni al-sirri, “for the hiding of the secret”: li- names what one is fit for. For a moment the tale is told in the third person again (“the slave-girl said to the jeweller”) before the jeweller takes up his own story. سيدتى is printed with final ى.

sentences.t: فَامْضِ وَتَوَجَّهْ يَاسَيِّدِى إِلَى عَلِيِّ بْنِ بَكَّارٍ سَرِيعًا وَأَخْبِرْهُ بِذَلِكَ لِأَجْلِ أَنْ يَكُونَ عَلَى أُهْبَةٍ وَحَذَرٍ
sentences.tr: fa-imḍi wa-tawajjah yā sayyidī ilā ʿAliyyi ibni Bakkārin sarīʿan wa-akhbirhu bi-dhālika li-ajli an yakūna ʿalā uhbatin wa-ḥadharin
sentences.l: So go and head, O my-master, to ʿAlī ibn Bakkār quickly, and inform-him of-that, for-the-sake (of it) that he-be upon readiness and caution;
sentences.i: So go, sir, make your way quickly to ʿAlī ibn Bakkār and tell him of this, so that he may be ready and on his guard;
sentences.n: imḍi, imperative of maḍā, “go”; tawajjah, imperative of tawajjaha, Form V, “turn one's face to”, make for. akhbara bi-, “to inform of”: bi- marks the thing told. li-ajli an, “for the sake of (it) that”, so that, with the subjunctive. ʿalā uhbatin wa-ḥadharin, “upon readiness and wariness”, ready and on guard. The print runs yā and sayyidī together (ياسيدى) and sets final ى; both are kept.

sentences.t: فَإِذَا انْكَشَفَ الْأَمْرُ نَتَدَبَّرُ فِي أَمْرٍ نَفْعَلُهُ لِنَجَاةِ أَنْفُسِنَا
sentences.tr: fa-idhā inkashafa al-amru natadabbaru fī amrin nafʿaluhu li-najāti anfusinā
sentences.l: and if the affair is-uncovered, we-take-thought in an-affair we-do-it for the-saving-of our-selves.
sentences.i: and if the matter comes to light, we will think out something to do to save ourselves.”
sentences.n: inkashafa, Form VII, “to be uncovered”, come out. The answer to idhā is a bare imperfect, natadabbaru, “we (will) take thought”: Classical more often answers idhā with a perfect, but an affirmative imperfect is allowed and, unlike an imperative or a nominal clause, needs no fa-. The “we” is the girl, her mistress and the men together. amrin nafʿaluhu, “a thing we may do”: an indefinite noun takes its relative clause without alladhī, and -hu takes up amr. najāt, “escape, safety”; anfus, plural of nafs, “self”.

sentences.t: قَالَ الْجَوْهَرِيُّ فَأَخَذَنِي مِنْ ذَلِكَ هَمٌّ عَظِيمٌ وَصَارَ الْكَوْنُ فِي وَجْهِي ظَلَامًا مِنْ كَلَامِ الْجَارِيَةِ
sentences.tr: qāla al-jawhariyyu fa-akhadhanī min dhālika hammun ʿaẓīmun wa-ṣāra al-kawnu fī wajhī ẓalāman min kalāmi al-jāriyati
sentences.l: The jeweller said: And there-took-me from that a great care, and the world became in my-face darkness from the words of the slave-girl.
sentences.i: The jeweller said: At this a great dread took hold of me, and at the slave-girl's words the world turned dark before my face.
sentences.n: akhadhanī … hammun, “a care took me”: the feeling is the subject and the man its object. ṣāra, “to become”, takes its predicate in the accusative, ẓalāman, “darkness”. al-kawn, “being”, here the whole world around him. The shadda of همّ is printed.

sentences.t: وَهَمَّتِ الْجَارِيَةُ لِتَمْضِيَ فَقُلْتُ لَهَا وَمَا الرَّأْيُ وَمَابَقِيَ فِى الْأَمْرِ وَقْتٌ
sentences.tr: wa-hammati al-jāriyatu li-tamḍiya fa-qultu lahā wa-mā al-raʾyu wa-mā baqiya fī al-amri waqtun
sentences.l: And the slave-girl made to-go; and I-said to-her: And what (is) the counsel? And there-has-not remained in the affair time.
sentences.i: The slave-girl made to go, and I said to her, “What is to be done, then? There is no time left in this business.”
sentences.n: hamma, “to set about, be on the point of”, here takes li- with the subjunctive, li-tamḍiya, “to go”. The two mā are different words: wa-mā al-raʾyu, “and what is the counsel?”, asks; wa-mā baqiya … waqtun, “and no time has remained”, denies. raʾy, “opinion”, is the everyday word for a plan, what is to be done. The print runs mā and baqiya together (ومابقي) and sets فى with final ى; the shadda of همّت and the hamza of الرأي are printed.

sentences.t: فَقَالَتْ لِي الرَّأْيُ أَنْ تُبَادِرَ إِلَى عَلِيِّ بْنِ بَكَّارٍ إِنْ كَانَ صَدِيقَكَ وَأَنْتَ تُرِيدُ لَهُ النَّجَاةَ
sentences.tr: fa-qālat lī al-raʾyu an tubādira ilā ʿAliyyi ibni Bakkārin in kāna ṣadīqaka wa-anta turīdu lahu al-najāta
sentences.l: And she-said to-me: The counsel (is) that you-hasten to ʿAlī ibn Bakkār, if he-is your-friend and you want for-him the escape.
sentences.i: She said to me, “What is to be done is this: go straight to ʿAlī ibn Bakkār, if he is your friend and you wish him to escape.
sentences.n: al-raʾyu an tubādira, “the counsel is that you hasten”: an with the subjunctive makes a clause that serves as the predicate. bādara ilā, Form III, “to hasten to”. wa-anta turīdu, “and you want”, a circumstantial clause with wa- and a pronoun. The hamza of الرأي is printed.

sentences.t: وَأَنْتَ عَلَيْكَ بِتَبْلِيغِ هَذَا الْخَبَرِ لَهُ بِسُرْعَةٍ وَلَا تُطَوِّلْ عَلَيْهِ هَذِهِ الْمُدَّةَ وَلَا تُبْعِدِ الْمَسَافَةَ
sentences.tr: wa-anta ʿalayka bi-tablīghi hādhā al-khabari lahu bi-surʿatin wa-lā tuṭawwil ʿalayhi hādhihi al-muddata wa-lā tubʿidi al-masāfata
sentences.l: And you — on-you (is) the conveying of this news to-him with speed; and do-not lengthen upon-him this period, and do-not make-far the distance.
sentences.i: For your part, see to it that this news reaches him quickly; do not keep him waiting long, or let the road stretch out.
sentences.n: wa-anta ʿalayka bi-…, “and you, on you is …”: anta is set at the head and then left hanging, a spoken way of saying “as for you”. ʿalayka bi-, “it is upon you to”, see to: bi- marks the thing one is charged with. tablīgh, Form II verbal noun of ballagha, “to convey”. The two prohibitions are read as jussives with objects: lā tuṭawwil ʿalayhi al-muddata, “do not draw out the time on him”, keep him waiting, and lā tubʿidi al-masāfata, “do not make the distance far”: both say hurry. tubʿid takes a helping -i before al-. The letters also allow wa-lā taṭūlu ʿalayhi hādhihi al-muddatu wa-lā tabʿudu al-masāfatu, “and this time will not be long for him, nor the distance far”, with the time and the distance as subjects. A wish, “let it not be long”, would need the jussive taṭul, which the printed و of تطول rules out.

sentences.t: وَأَنَا عَلَيَّ أَنْ أَتَقَيَّدَ بِاسْتِنْشَاقِ الْأَخْبَارِ
sentences.tr: wa-anā ʿalayya an ataqayyada bi-istinshāqi al-akhbāri
sentences.l: And I — on-me (is) that I-bind-myself to the sniffing-out of the news.
sentences.i: As for me, it falls to me to make it my task to scent out the news.”
sentences.n: wa-anā ʿalayya an …, “and I, on me is that …”, the girl's own share, built like the jeweller's. taqayyada bi-, Form V, “to bind oneself to”, take on as a duty. istinshāq, Form X verbal noun from the root of “to sniff”, used of nosing out news. The shadda of عليّ is printed.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ وَدَّعَتْنِي وَخَرَجَتْ
sentences.tr: thumma waddaʿatnī wa-kharajat
sentences.l: Then she-bade-farewell-to-me and went-out.
sentences.i: Then she took her leave of me and went out.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا خَرَجَتِ الْجَارِيَةُ قُمْتُ وَخَرَجْتُ فِي أَثَرِهَا وَمَضَيْتُ إِلَى عَلِيِّ بْنِ بَكَّارٍ فَوَجَدْتُهُ يُمَنِّي نَفْسَهُ بِالْوِصَالِ وَيُعَلِّلُهَا بِالْمُحَالِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā kharajati al-jāriyatu qumtu wa-kharajtu fī atharihā wa-maḍaytu ilā ʿAliyyi ibni Bakkārin fa-wajadtuhu yumannī nafsahu bi-al-wiṣāli wa-yuʿalliluhā bi-al-muḥāli
sentences.l: And when the slave-girl went-out, I-rose and went-out in her-track, and went to ʿAlī ibn Bakkār; and I-found-him feeding-with-hopes his-self with the union, and soothing-it with the impossible.
sentences.i: When the slave-girl had gone, I got up and went out after her, and made my way to ʿAlī ibn Bakkār. I found him feeding himself on hopes of union, and soothing his heart with what could never be.
sentences.n: fī atharihā, “in her track”, straight after her. mannā nafsahu bi-, Form II, “to feed one's soul with the hope of”; ʿallala bi-, Form II, “to divert, put off with”: the -hā of yuʿalliluhā is his nafs, feminine. The rhymed pair wiṣāl / muḥāl, “union / the impossible”, is sajʿ, and the rhyme runs on through the next two sentences (al-ḥāl, al-muṭāl, al-ishtighāl). The shaddas of يمنّي and يعلّلها are printed.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا رَآنِي رَجَعْتُ إِلَيْهِ عَاجِلًا قَالَ لِي إِنِّي أَرَاكَ رَجَعْتَ إِلَيَّ وَجِئْتَ فِى الْحَالِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā raʾānī rajaʿtu ilayhi ʿājilan qāla lī innī arāka rajaʿta ilayya wa-jiʾta fī al-ḥāli
sentences.l: And when he-saw-me — I-had-returned to-him quickly — he-said to-me: (Indeed) I see-you you-have-returned to-me and come at the instant.
sentences.i: When he saw me come back to him so soon, he said to me, “I see you have come back to me, and straightaway.”
sentences.n: raʾānī rajaʿtu ilayhi, “he saw me, I had returned to him”: the second verb stands loose, with no joining word, describing what he saw; arāka rajaʿta, “I see you, you have returned”, is built the same way. ʿājilan, “hastily”, an adverbial accusative. fī al-ḥāli, “in the moment”, at once. The madda of رآني and the shadda of اليّ are printed; فى is printed with final ى.

sentences.t: فَقُلْتُ لَهُ اصْبِرْ أَتْصِرْ مِنَ التَّعَلُّقِ الْمُطَالِ وَدَعْ مَا أَنْتَ فِيهِ مِنَ الِاشْتِغَالِ
sentences.tr: fa-qultu lahu iṣbir atṣir mina al-taʿalluqi al-muṭāli wa-daʿ mā anta fīhi mina al-ishtighāli
sentences.l: And I-said to-him: Be-patient, [desist] from the drawn-out attachment, and leave what you (are) in-it of the preoccupation;
sentences.i: I said to him, “Bear up, and break off this long-drawn-out attachment; leave what you are busy with.
sentences.n: The print has اتصر, which is not an Arabic word. It is kept, and vocalised on the pattern of aqṣir, “desist!” (Form IV of qaṣara, used with ʿan or min), the likeliest reading, with ق set as ت; iqtaṣir or ikhtaṣir, “cut it short”, are also possible. The sense, “break off”, is clear either way. iṣbir, imperative of ṣabara, “be patient”, bear up. daʿ, imperative of wadaʿa, “let be”: mā anta fīhi, “what you are in”, the state he is wrapped up in. muṭāl, passive participle of aṭāla, Form IV, “drawn out”. The sajʿ goes on: muṭāl / ishtighāl.

sentences.t: فَقَدْ حَدَثَ حَادِثٌ وَأَمْرٌ فِيهِ إِتْلَافُ نَفْسِكَ وَمَالِكَ
sentences.tr: fa-qad ḥadatha ḥādithun wa-amrun fīhi itlāfu nafsika wa-mālika
sentences.l: For there-has-happened a-happening, and an-affair in-it (is) the destruction of your-self and your-wealth.
sentences.i: Something has happened, a business that will cost you your life and your fortune.”
sentences.n: ḥadatha ḥādithun, “a happening has happened”: the verb with a noun from its own root, a common way of saying “something has come up”. amrun fīhi itlāfu …, “an affair in which is the destruction of …”: an indefinite noun with its relative clause, no alladhī. itlāf, Form IV verbal noun of talifa, “to perish”: “making perish”, ruin.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعَ هَذَا الْكَلَامَ تَغَيَّرَ حَالُهُ وَانْزَعَجَ وَقَالَ لِي يَا أَخِي أَخْبِرْنِي بِمَاوَقَعَ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿa hādhā al-kalāma taghayyara ḥāluhu wa-inzaʿaja wa-qāla lī yā akhī akhbirnī bi-mā waqaʿa
sentences.l: And when he-heard this speech, his-state changed and he-was-alarmed, and he-said to-me: O my-brother, inform-me of-what happened.
sentences.i: When he heard this his colour changed and he was alarmed, and he said to me, “Brother, tell me what has happened.”
sentences.n: taghayyara ḥāluhu, “his state changed”, he changed countenance. inzaʿaja, Form VII, “to be disturbed”, alarmed. akhbara bi-, “to inform of”. The print runs bi-mā and waqaʿa together (بماوقع); it is kept as one word.

sentences.t: فَقُلْتُ لَهُ يَا سَيِّدِي اعْلَمْ أَنَّهُ قَدْ جَرَى مَاهُوَ كَذَا وَكَذَا وَأَنَّكَ تَالِفٌ لَامَحَالَةَ إِنْ أَقَمْتَ فِي دَارِكَ هَذِهِ إِلَى آخِرِ النَّهَارِ
sentences.tr: fa-qultu lahu yā sayyidī iʿlam annahu qad jarā mā huwa kadhā wa-kadhā wa-annaka tālifun lā maḥālata in aqamta fī dārika hādhihi ilā ākhiri al-nahāri
sentences.l: And I-said to-him: O my-master, know that-it (is that) there-has-happened what it (is) such and such, and that-you (are) perishing, no escape, if you-stay in this your-house until the end of the day.
sentences.i: I said to him, “Sir, you must know that such and such has happened, and that you are a dead man, beyond all doubt, if you stay in this house of yours until the end of the day.”
sentences.n: iʿlam, “know!”, the usual opening to grave news. kadhā wa-kadhā, “such and such”: the teller does not repeat what the reader already knows. tālif, “perishing”, done for. lā maḥālata, “there is no avoiding (it)”, inevitably: lā denying all, its noun in -a. dārika hādhihi, “this house of yours”: the demonstrative follows a noun made definite by its suffix. The print runs mā huwa and lā maḥālata together (ماهو, لامحالة); they are kept so. The madda of آخر is printed.

sentences.t: فَبُهِتَ عَلِيُّ بْنُ بَكَّارٍ وَكَادَتْ رُوحُهُ أَنْ تُفَارِقَ جَسَدَهُ
sentences.tr: fa-buhita ʿAliyyu ibnu Bakkārin wa-kādat rūḥuhu an tufāriqa jasadahu
sentences.l: And ʿAlī ibn Bakkār was-dumbfounded, and his-soul was-about that it-part-from his-body.
sentences.i: ʿAlī ibn Bakkār was struck dumb, and his soul all but left his body.
sentences.n: buhita, “was dumbfounded”, passive in form (bahita is also found). kāda, “to be on the point of”, here with an and the subjunctive, which Classical allows but does not prefer after kāda. rūḥ, “soul”, is feminine, hence kādat and tufāriqa.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ اسْتَرْجَعَ بَعْدَ ذَلِكَ وَقَالَ لِي أَيَّ شَيْءٍ أَفْعَلُ يَا أَخِي وَمَا عِنْدَكَ مِنَ الرَّأْيِ
sentences.tr: thumma istarjaʿa baʿda dhālika wa-qāla lī ayya shayʾin afʿalu yā akhī wa-mā ʿindaka mina al-raʾyi
sentences.l: Then he-recovered after that, and said to-me: What thing do-I-do, O my-brother, and what (is) with-you of the counsel?
sentences.i: Then, after a while, he collected himself and said to me, “What am I to do, brother? What do you advise?”
sentences.n: istarjaʿa, Form X of rajaʿa, is properly “to say innā li-llāhi wa-innā ilayhi rājiʿūna”, “we are God's and to Him we return”, the words spoken at a calamity; from that it comes to mean pulling oneself together after a blow, and either sense fits here. ayya shayʾin afʿalu, “which thing shall I do”: ayya is the object, set first. mā ʿindaka mina al-raʾyi, “what have you of counsel”: min marks the kind of thing asked for. The hamza of شيء and of الرأي is printed.

sentences.t: فَقُلْتُ لَهُ الرَّأْيُ خُذْ مَعَكَ مِنْ مَالِكَ مَاتَقْدِرُ عَلَيْهِ وَمِنْ غِلْمَانِكَ مَاتَثِقُ بِهِ وَامْضِ بِنَا إِلَى دِيَارٍ غَيْرِ هَذِهِ قَبْلَ أَنْ يَنْقَضِيَ هَذَا النَّهَارُ
sentences.tr: fa-qultu lahu al-raʾyu khudh maʿaka min mālika mā taqdiru ʿalayhi wa-min ghilmānika mā tathiqu bihi wa-imḍi binā ilā diyārin ghayri hādhihi qabla an yanqaḍiya hādhā al-nahāru
sentences.l: And I-said to-him: The counsel: take with-you of your-wealth what you-are-able for-it, and of your-lads what you-trust in-it, and go with-us to abodes other-than these, before that this day comes-to-an-end.
sentences.i: I said to him, “My advice is this: take with you as much of your wealth as you can manage, and those of your servants you can trust, and let us be off to some other place before this day is out.”
sentences.n: al-raʾyu khudh, “the counsel: take!”: the imperative itself stands as the predicate, without an. mā taqdiru ʿalayhi, “what you are able for”; mā tathiqu bihi, “what you trust”: mā is used even for the servants, people, where Classical would want man. imḍi binā, “go with us”: maḍā bi-, “to go off with”, the jeweller including himself. diyārin ghayri hādhihi, “lands other than these”: ghayr agrees in case with the noun before it. The print runs mā taqdiru and mā tathiqu together (ماتقدر, ماتثق); they are kept so. The hamza of الرأي is printed.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لِي سَمْعًا وَطَاعَةً
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lī samʿan wa-ṭāʿatan
sentences.l: And he-said to-me: Hearing and obedience.
sentences.i: “With hearing and obedience,” he said to me.

sentences.t: فَوَثَبَ عَلِيُّ بْنُ بَكَّارٍ وَهُوَ مُتَخَبِّلٌ وَمُتَحَيِّرٌ فِي أَمْرِهِ فَتَارَةً يَمْشِي وَتَارَةً يَقَعُ
sentences.tr: fa-wathaba ʿAliyyu ibnu Bakkārin wa-huwa mutakhabbilun wa-mutaḥayyirun fī amrihi fa-tāratan yamshī wa-tāratan yaqaʿu
sentences.l: And ʿAlī ibn Bakkār leapt-up, and he (was) distracted and bewildered in his-affair; and one-time he-walks and one-time he-falls.
sentences.i: ʿAlī ibn Bakkār sprang up, out of his wits and not knowing what to do; one moment he walked, the next he fell down.
sentences.n: wathaba, “to leap up”. wa-huwa mutakhabbilun, “he being distracted”, a circumstantial clause; mutakhabbil, Form V participle from khabl, “derangement”. tāratan … wa-tāratan, “one time … and one time”, now … now; the imperfects yamshī and yaqaʿu describe what kept happening.

sentences.t: فَأَخَذَ مَا قَدَرَ عَلَيْهِ وَاعْتَذَرَ إِلَى أَهْلِهِ وَأَوْصَاهُمْ بِمَقْصُودِهِ وَأَخَذَ مَعَهُ ثَلٰثَةَ جِمَالٍ مُحَمَّلَةٍ وَرَكِبَ دَابَّتَهُ وَقَدْ فَعَلْتُ أَنَا كَمَا فَعَلَ
sentences.tr: fa-akhadha mā qadara ʿalayhi wa-iʿtadhara ilā ahlihi wa-awṣāhum bi-maqṣūdihi wa-akhadha maʿahu thalāthata jimālin muḥammalatin wa-rakiba dābbatahu wa-qad faʿaltu anā kamā faʿala
sentences.l: And he-took what he-was-able for-it, and excused-himself to his-family, and charged-them with his-intention; and he-took with-him three camels laden, and mounted his-beast; and I had-done, I, as he-did.
sentences.i: He took what he could, made his excuses to his household and left them his instructions, took three loaded camels with him and mounted his beast; and I did as he did.
sentences.n: iʿtadhara ilā, Form VIII, “to make one's excuses to”. awṣā bi-, Form IV, “to charge with, leave instructions about”: bi- marks the matter. thalāthata jimālin: a numeral from three to ten takes the genitive plural, with -a because jamal is masculine. muḥammala, passive participle of ḥammala, Form II, “loaded”. wa-qad faʿaltu anā, “and I had done”, with anā underlining the “I”. ثلٰثة is printed with the dagger alif, the edition's own spelling of thalātha.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ خَرَجْنَا خُفْيَةً وَنَحْنُ مُتَنَكِّرُونَ وَسِرْنَا وَلَمْ نَزَلْ مُسَافِرِينَ بَاقِيَ يَوْمِنَا وَلَيْلَتِنَا
sentences.tr: thumma kharajnā khufyatan wa-naḥnu mutanakkirūna wa-sirnā wa-lam nazal musāfirīna bāqiya yawminā wa-laylatinā
sentences.l: Then we-went-out in-secret, and we (were) disguised, and we-travelled, and we-did-not cease travelling the rest of our-day and our-night.
sentences.i: Then we slipped out secretly, in disguise, and set off, and kept travelling the rest of that day and the night.
sentences.n: khufyatan, “in secret”, an adverbial accusative. lam nazal, “we did not cease”, with the participle musāfirīna in the accusative as its predicate: “we kept on travelling”. bāqiya yawminā, “the rest of our day”, accusative of time. The shadda of متنكّرون is printed.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا كَانَ آخِرُ اللَّيْلِ حَطَطْنَا حُمُولَنَا وَعَقَلْنَا جِمَالَنَا وَنِمْنَا فَحَلَّ عَلَيْنَا التَّعَبُ وَغَفَلْنَا عَنْ أَنْفُسِنَا
sentences.tr: fa-lammā kāna ākhiru al-layli ḥaṭaṭnā ḥumūlanā wa-ʿaqalnā jimālanā wa-nimnā fa-ḥalla ʿalaynā al-taʿabu wa-ghafalnā ʿan anfusinā
sentences.l: And when it-was the end of the night, we-set-down our-loads and hobbled our-camels and slept; and the weariness came-down upon-us, and we-were-heedless of our-selves.
sentences.i: Towards the end of the night we set down our loads, hobbled our camels and lay down to sleep; weariness overcame us, and we lost all heed of ourselves.
sentences.n: ḥaṭaṭnā: the doubled verb ḥaṭṭa keeps its two ṭāʾs apart before a consonant ending, as Classical does. ʿaqala, “to hobble” a camel by tying up a foreleg. nimnā, from nāma, “to sleep”. ḥalla ʿalā, “to come down upon”, used of a misfortune or a state. The madda of آخر and the shadda of فحلّ are printed.

sentences.t: وَإِذَا بِاللُّصُوصِ أَحَاطُوا بِنَا وَأَخَذُوا جَمِيعَ مَا كَانَ مَعَنَا وَقَتَلُوا الْغِلْمَانَ لَمَّا أَرَادُوا أَنْ يَمْنَعُوا عَنَّا
sentences.tr: wa-idhā bi-al-luṣūṣi aḥāṭū binā wa-akhadhū jamīʿa mā kāna maʿanā wa-qatalū al-ghilmāna lammā arādū an yamnaʿū ʿannā
sentences.l: And behold, the robbers surrounded us, and took all that was with-us, and killed the lads when they-wanted that they-defend from-us.
sentences.i: And suddenly the robbers were all around us. They took everything we had with us, and killed the servants when they tried to defend us.
sentences.n: wa-idhā bi-, “and behold”: bi- only marks what appears. aḥāṭa bi-, Form IV, “to surround”. manaʿa ʿan, “to keep off from”, here with no object expressed: to keep the robbers off us, to defend us. lammā with the perfect, “when”. The shadda of عنّا is printed.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ تَرَكُونَا مَكَانَنَا وَنَحْنُ فِي أَقْبَحِ حَالٍ بَعْدَ أَنْ أَخَذُوا الْمَالَ وَسَاقُوا الْجَمِيعَ وَسَارُوا
sentences.tr: thumma tarakūnā makānanā wa-naḥnu fī aqbaḥi ḥālin baʿda an akhadhū al-māla wa-sāqū al-jamīʿa wa-sārū
sentences.l: Then they-left-us (in) our-place, and we (were) in the ugliest state, after that they-took the goods and drove-off the whole and went.
sentences.i: Then they left us where we were, in the sorriest plight, after they had taken the goods and driven everything off, and went their way.
sentences.n: makānanā, “our place”, an accusative of place: where we lay. fī aqbaḥi ḥālin, “in the ugliest of states”: an elative before an indefinite singular noun is a superlative. sāqa, “to drive (beasts)”: al-jamīʿ, “the whole lot”, the camels with their loads and the mounts.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا قُمْنَا مَشَيْنَا إِلَى أَنْ أَصْبَحَ الصَّبَاحُ فَوَصَلْنَا إِلَى بَلَدٍ فَدَخَلْنَاهَا
sentences.tr: fa-lammā qumnā mashaynā ilā an aṣbaḥa al-ṣabāḥu fa-waṣalnā ilā baladin fa-dakhalnāhā
sentences.l: And when we-rose, we-walked until that the morning dawned, and we-arrived at a-town and entered-it,
sentences.i: When we got up we walked on until morning came, and reached a town and went in,
sentences.n: ilā an aṣbaḥa al-ṣabāḥu, “until the morning dawned”: ilā an with the perfect, of a thing that did happen. balad, “town”, is masculine, but the pronoun of dakhalnāhā is feminine, as if the teller had in mind balda, the word the travellers use for the place below.

sentences.t: وَقَصَدْنَا مَسْجِدَهَا فَدَخَلْنَا إِلَيْهِ وَنَحْنُ عُرْيَانُونَ
sentences.tr: wa-qaṣadnā masjidahā fa-dakhalnā ilayhi wa-naḥnu ʿuryānūna
sentences.l: and made-for its-mosque, and entered into-it, and we (were) naked.
sentences.i: and made for its mosque and went in, naked as we were.
sentences.n: dakhala ilā, “to go into”; Classical more often has dakhala with a direct object. ʿuryānūna, “naked”, is the sound plural of ʿuryān, its regular plural in Classical Arabic too (ʿurāh is the plural of the synonym ʿārin): the robbers have taken their clothes with everything else.

sentences.t: فَجَلَسْنَا فِي جَانِبِ الْمَسْجِدِ بَاقِيَ يَوْمِنَا كُلَّهُ فَلَمَّا جَاءَ اللَّيْلُ بِتْنَا فِيهِ تِلْكَ اللَّيْلَةَ وَنَحْنُ بِغَيْرِ أَكْلٍ وَشُرْبٍ
sentences.tr: fa-jalasnā fī jānibi al-masjidi bāqiya yawminā kullahu fa-lammā jāʾa al-laylu bitnā fīhi tilka al-laylata wa-naḥnu bi-ghayri aklin wa-shurbin
sentences.l: And we-sat in a side of the mosque the rest of our-day, all-of-it; and when the night came, we-passed-the-night in-it, that night, and we (were) without eating and drinking.
sentences.i: We sat in a corner of the mosque for the whole of the rest of that day; and when night came we spent it there, without food or drink.
sentences.n: bitnā, from bāta, “to pass the night”; tilka al-laylata, “that night”, accusative of time; fīhi is the mosque. bi-ghayri, “without”: bi- with ghayr, “other than”, makes “with other than”. The hamza of جاء is printed.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا أَصْبَحَ الصَّبَاحُ صَلَّيْنَا الصُّبْحَ وَجَلَسْنَا
sentences.tr: fa-lammā aṣbaḥa al-ṣabāḥu ṣallaynā al-ṣubḥa wa-jalasnā
sentences.l: And when the morning dawned, we-prayed the dawn (prayer) and sat.
sentences.i: When morning came we prayed the dawn prayer and sat on.
sentences.n: al-ṣubḥ, “dawn”, here the dawn prayer, the object of ṣallaynā. The shadda of صلّينا is printed.

sentences.t: وَإِذَا بِرَجُلٍ دَخَلَ وَسَلَّمَ عَلَيْنَا وَصَلَّى رَكْعَتَيْنِ ثُمَّ الْتَفَتَ إِلَيْنَا وَقَالَ يَا جَمَاعَةُ هَلْ أَنْتُمْ غُرَبَاءُ
sentences.tr: wa-idhā bi-rajulin dakhala wa-sallama ʿalaynā wa-ṣallā rakʿatayni thumma iltafata ilaynā wa-qāla yā jamāʿatu hal antum ghurabāʾu
sentences.l: And behold, a-man entered and greeted us and prayed two-rakʿas; then he-turned to-us and said: O company, are you strangers?
sentences.i: And then a man came in, greeted us and prayed two rakʿas; then he turned to us and said, “Good people, are you strangers here?”
sentences.n: wa-idhā bi-rajulin, “and behold, a man”: bi- marks what appears. sallama ʿalā, Form II, “to greet”. rakʿatayni, dual of rakʿa, one round of bowing and prostration in the prayer. yā jamāʿatu, “O company”: the noun addressed takes -u. ghurabāʾ, plural of gharīb, “stranger”, is diptote, so -u without tanwīn. The shadda of صلّى and the hamza of غرباء are printed.

sentences.t: قُلْنَا نَعَمْ وَقَطَعَ اللُّصُوصُ عَلَيْنَا الطَّرِيقَ وَعَرَّوْنَا وَدَخَلْنَا هَذِهِ الْبَلْدَةَ وَلَمْ نَعْرِفْ فِيهَا أَحَدًا نَأْوِي عِنْدَهُ
sentences.tr: qulnā naʿam wa-qaṭaʿa al-luṣūṣu ʿalaynā al-ṭarīqa wa-ʿarrawnā wa-dakhalnā hādhihi al-baldata wa-lam naʿrif fīhā aḥadan naʾwī ʿindahu
sentences.l: We-said: Yes; and the robbers cut upon-us the road, and stripped-us, and we-entered this town, and we-did-not know in-it anyone we-shelter with-him.
sentences.i: We said, “Yes. Robbers waylaid us on the road and stripped us, and we have come into this town knowing no one here we can go to for shelter.”
sentences.n: qaṭaʿa ʿalā fulānin al-ṭarīqa, “to cut the road on someone”, to waylay. The verb stands first and singular before its plural subject al-luṣūṣ, as Classical requires. ʿarrā, Form II of ʿariya, “to strip”. aḥadan naʾwī ʿindahu, “anyone we might shelter with”: an indefinite noun with its relative clause, ʿindahu taking it up. The shadda of عرّونا and the hamza of نأوي are printed.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَنَا الرَّجُلُ هَلْ لَكُمْ أَنْ تَقُومُوا مَعِي إِلَى دَارِي
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lanā al-rajulu hal lakum an taqūmū maʿī ilā dārī
sentences.l: And the man said to-us: Is (there) for-you that you-rise with-me to my-house?
sentences.i: The man said to us, “Will you come with me to my house?”
sentences.n: hal lakum an …, “is it for you that …”, the polite way of asking whether someone would like to do a thing. qāma, “to rise”, here to get up and come along.

sentences.t: قَالَ الْجَوْهَرِيُّ فَقُلْتُ لِعَلِيِّ بْنِ بَكَّارٍ قُمْ بِنَا مَعَهُ
sentences.tr: qāla al-jawhariyyu fa-qultu li-ʿAliyyi ibni Bakkārin qum binā maʿahu
sentences.l: The jeweller said: And I-said to ʿAlī ibn Bakkār: Rise with-us with-him,
sentences.i: The jeweller said: I said to ʿAlī ibn Bakkār, “Come, let us go with him,
sentences.n: qum binā, “rise with us”, let us go: qāma bi-, “to rise with”, the jeweller including himself. li- marks the one spoken to.

sentences.t: فَنَنْجُوَ مِنْ أَمْرَيْنِ الْأَوَّلُ أَنَّنَا نَخْشَي أَنْ يَدْخُلَ عَلَيْنَا أَحَدٌ إِلَى هَذَا الْمَسْجِدِ فَيَعْرِفَنَا فَنَفْتَضِحَ وَالثَّانِي أَنَّنَا نَاسٌ غُرَبَاءُ وَلَيْسَ لَنَا مَحَلٌّ نَأْوِي إِلَيْهِ
sentences.tr: fa-nanjuwa min amrayni al-awwalu annanā nakhshā an yadkhula ʿalaynā aḥadun ilā hādhā al-masjidi fa-yaʿrifanā fa-naftaḍiḥa wa-al-thānī annanā nāsun ghurabāʾu wa-laysa lanā maḥallun naʾwī ilayhi
sentences.l: so-that we-escape from two-things: the first, that-we fear that someone enter upon-us into this mosque and know-us, and we-be-disgraced; and the second, that-we (are) people, strangers, and there-is-not for-us a-place we-take-refuge to-it.”
sentences.i: so that we may escape two dangers. The first is that we are afraid someone may come in on us here in this mosque and recognise us, and we shall be found out; the second is that we are strangers and have nowhere to shelter.”
sentences.n: This finishes the jeweller's words to ʿAlī. fa-nanjuwa is read as the subjunctive after fa- that answers a command (“come with us … so that we escape”); the letters equally allow the indicative fa-nanjū, “and we shall escape”. al-awwalu … wa-al-thānī, “the first … and the second”, each followed by its clause. نخشي is printed with ي for final ى (nakhshā). dakhala ʿalā, “to come in on (someone)”; ilā hādhā al-masjidi, “into this mosque”. fa-yaʿrifanā fa-naftaḍiḥa carry on the subjunctive of an yadkhula; iftaḍaḥa, Form VIII of faḍaḥa, “to be disgraced, exposed”. ghurabāʾ, plural of gharīb, “stranger”, is diptote. awā ilā, “to take refuge in”: maḥallun naʾwī ilayhi, “a place we may shelter in”, an indefinite noun with its relative clause and no alladhī, ilayhi taking up the place. The hamza of نأوي is printed.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ عَلِيُّ بْنُ بَكَّارٍ افْعَلْ مَاتُرِيدُ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla ʿAliyyu ibnu Bakkārin ifʿal mā turīdu
sentences.l: And ʿAlī ibn Bakkār said: Do what you-want.
sentences.i: ʿAlī ibn Bakkār said, “Do as you think best.”
sentences.n: ifʿal, imperative of faʿala, “to do”. ماتريد is printed as one word: mā turīdu, “what you want”.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّ الرَّجُلَ قَالَ لَنَا ثَانِيَ مَرَّةٍ يَا فُقَرَاءُ أَطِيعُونِي وَسِيرُوا مَعِي إِلَى مَكَانِي
sentences.tr: thumma inna al-rajula qāla lanā thāniya marratin yā fuqarāʾu aṭīʿūnī wa-sīrū maʿī ilā makānī
sentences.l: Then (indeed) the man said to-us a-second time: O poor-ones, obey-me and go with-me to my-place.
sentences.i: Then the man said to us a second time, “Poor fellows, do as I say and come with me to my house.”
sentences.n: thumma inna …, “then (it was that) …”, the narrator's usual way of moving on; inna puts al-rajula in the accusative. thāniya marratin, “the second of a time”, a second time, an adverbial accusative. fuqarāʾ, plural of faqīr, “poor man”, also a beggar: robbed and stripped, the two look destitute. yā fuqarāʾu, vocative, nominative without tanwīn. aṭāʿa, Form IV, “to obey”; sāra, “to go”.

sentences.t: قَالَ الْجَوْهَرِيُّ فَقُلْتُ لَهُ السَّمْعُ وَالطَّاعَةُ
sentences.tr: qāla al-jawhariyyu fa-qultu lahu al-samʿu wa-al-ṭāʿatu
sentences.l: The jeweller said: And I-said to-him: The hearing and the obedience.
sentences.i: The jeweller said: I answered him, “Hearing and obedience.”
sentences.n: qāla al-jawhariyyu, “the jeweller said”, reminds the reader whose story this is: the jeweller is telling it, and the fa- of fa-qultu picks up his own narration. al-samʿu wa-al-ṭāʿatu, “hearing and obedience”, the stock formula of assent.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّ الرَّجُلَ خَلَعَ عَلَيْنَا شَيْأً مِنْ أَثْوَابِهِ وَأَلْبَسَنَا وَاعْتَذَرَ لَنَا وَلَاطَفَنَا
sentences.tr: thumma inna al-rajula khalaʿa ʿalaynā shayʾan min athwābihi wa-albasanā wa-iʿtadhara lanā wa-lāṭafanā
sentences.l: Then (indeed) the man cast upon-us something of his-garments and clothed-us, and excused-himself to-us and treated-us-kindly.
sentences.i: Then the man gave us some of his own clothes and dressed us, and made his excuses to us and was kind to us.
sentences.n: khalaʿa ʿalā, “to take off (a garment) onto someone”, to bestow clothing; the robbers had stripped them. شيأ is the print's spelling of shayʾan, with the hamza printed. athwāb, plural of thawb, “garment”. albasa, Form IV of labisa, “to clothe”. iʿtadhara li-, “to apologise to”: li- marks the one apologised to. lāṭafa, Form III, “to treat kindly”.

sentences.t: فَقُمْنَا مَعَهُ إِلَى دَارِهِ فَطَرَقَ الْبَابَ فَخَرَجَ إِلَيْهِ خَادِمٌ صَغِيرٌ وَفَتَحَ الْبَابَ
sentences.tr: fa-qumnā maʿahu ilā dārihi fa-ṭaraqa al-bāba fa-kharaja ilayhi khādimun ṣaghīrun wa-fataḥa al-bāba
sentences.l: And we-rose with-him to his-house; and he-knocked the door, and there-came-out to-him a-servant small, and opened the door.
sentences.i: So we got up and went with him to his house. He knocked at the door, and a servant boy came out to him and opened it.
sentences.n: qāma ilā, “to rise (and go) to”. ṭaraqa al-bāba, “to knock at the door”, the door the direct object. khādimun ṣaghīrun, “a small servant”, a boy.

sentences.t: فَدَخَلَ الرَّجُلُ صَاحِبُ الْمَنْزِلِ وَدَخَلْنَا خَلْفَهُ
sentences.tr: fa-dakhala al-rajulu ṣāḥibu al-manzili wa-dakhalnā khalfahu
sentences.l: And the man, the owner of the dwelling, entered, and we-entered behind-him.
sentences.i: The man, the master of the house, went in, and we went in after him.
sentences.n: ṣāḥibu al-manzili, “the companion of the dwelling”, its owner, in apposition to al-rajulu. khalfahu, “behind him”, adverbial accusative.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّ الرَّجُلَ أَمَرَ بِإِحْضَارِ بُقْجَةٍ فِيهَا ثِيَابٌ وَشَاشَاتٌ فَأَلْبَسَنَا حُلَّتَيْنِ وَأَعْطَانَا شَاشَيْنِ فَتَعَمَّمْنَا وَجَلَسْنَا
sentences.tr: thumma inna al-rajula amara bi-iḥḍāri buqjatin fīhā thiyābun wa-shāshātun fa-albasanā ḥullatayni wa-aʿṭānā shāshayni fa-taʿammamnā wa-jalasnā
sentences.l: Then (indeed) the man ordered the bringing of a-bundle, in-it clothes and turban-cloths; and he-clothed-us (in) two-suits and gave-us two-turban-cloths, and we-put-on-turbans and sat.
sentences.i: Then the man ordered a bundle to be brought with clothes and turban-cloths in it. He dressed each of us in a suit of clothes and gave each a turban-cloth, and we wound our turbans and sat down.
sentences.n: amara bi-, “to order”: the verb chooses bi-, which marks the thing ordered. iḥḍār, verbal noun of Form IV aḥḍara, “to have (something) brought”. buqja, a cloth wrapper for clothes (from Turkish bohça); fīhā …, “in it …”, describes it. shāsh, plural shāshāt, fine muslin, the long cloth wound into a turban. ḥulla, a full suit of clothes; ḥullatayni and shāshayni are dual, one for each man. albasa here takes two objects, “clothed us (in) two suits”. taʿammama, Form V, “to put on a turban” (ʿimāma); the shadda of فتعمّمنا is printed.

sentences.t: وَإِذَا بِجَارِيَةٍ أَقْبَلَتْ إِلَيْنَا بِمَائِدَةٍ وَوَضَعَتْهَا بَيْنَ أَيْدِينَا وَقَالَتْ كُلُوا
sentences.tr: wa-idhā bi-jāriyatin aqbalat ilaynā bi-māʾidatin wa-waḍaʿathā bayna aydīnā wa-qālat kulū
sentences.l: And behold, a-slave-girl came-forward to-us with a-table, and set-it between our-hands, and said: Eat.
sentences.i: And now a slave-girl came up to us with a laden table, set it before us and said, “Eat.”
sentences.n: wa-idhā bi-, “and behold”: after idhā of surprise bi- only marks what appears. aqbala ilā, “to come towards”; the second bi-, bi-māʾidatin, marks what she brings. māʾida, a table or tray set with food; its hamza is printed. bayna aydīnā, “between our hands”, before us. kulū, plural imperative of akala, “to eat”.

sentences.t: فَأَكَلْنَا شَيْأً يَسِيرًا وَرَفَعَتِ الْمَائِدَةَ
sentences.tr: fa-akalnā shayʾan yasīran wa-rafaʿati al-māʾidata
sentences.l: And we-ate a-thing little, and she-raised the table.
sentences.i: We ate a little, and she cleared the table away.
sentences.n: yasīr, “slight, small”. رفعت is read rafaʿat, “she took up”, the slave-girl clearing the meal; rufiʿat al-māʾidatu, “the table was taken away”, is equally possible. rafaʿa al-māʾida, “to lift the table”, is the regular phrase for clearing food away.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ أَقَمْنَا عِنْدَهُ إِلَى أَنْ دَخَلَ اللَّيْلُ
sentences.tr: thumma aqamnā ʿindahu ilā an dakhala al-laylu
sentences.l: Then we-stayed with-him until that the night entered.
sentences.i: Then we stayed with him until night came on.
sentences.n: aqāma, Form IV, “to stay”. ilā an, “until”, here with the perfect for what did happen.

sentences.t: فَتَأَوَّهَ عَلِيُّ بْنُ بَكَّارٍ وَقَالَ لِلْجَوْهَرِيِّ اعْلَمْ يَا أَخِي أَنَّنِي هَالِكٌ لَا مَحَالَةَ
sentences.tr: fa-taʾawwaha ʿAliyyu ibnu Bakkārin wa-qāla li-al-jawhariyyi iʿlam yā akhī annanī hālikun lā maḥālata
sentences.l: And ʿAlī ibn Bakkār sighed “ah!” and said to-the jeweller: Know, O my-brother, that-I (am) perishing, no avoiding (it).
sentences.i: Then ʿAlī ibn Bakkār heaved a sigh and said to the jeweller, “Know, my brother, that I am surely a dead man.
sentences.n: taʾawwaha, Form V, “to say āh”, to sigh in pain; its hamza and shadda are printed. The narration slips into the third person, “said to the jeweller”, though the jeweller is telling the tale. iʿlam, “know”, the usual opening of a weighty statement. hālik, “perishing”. lā maḥālata, “there is no avoiding (it)”, inevitably: lā of absolute negation with its noun in the accusative, without tanwīn.

sentences.t: وَأُرِيدُ أَنْ أُوصِيَكَ بِوَصِيَّةٍ وَهُوَ أَنِّي إِذَا رَأَيْتَنِي مُتُّ اذْهَبْ إِلَى وَالِدَتِي وَأَخْبِرْهَا
sentences.tr: wa-urīdu an ūṣiyaka bi-waṣiyyatin wa-huwa annī idhā raʾaytanī muttu idhhab ilā wālidatī wa-akhbirhā
sentences.l: And I-want that I-charge-you with a-charge, and it (is) that-I — when you-see-me, I-have-died — go to my-mother and inform-her,
sentences.i: I want to leave you a last charge, and it is this: when you see that I have died, go to my mother and tell her;
sentences.n: awṣā, Form IV, “to charge, enjoin”, with bi- for the thing enjoined: ūṣiyaka bi-waṣiyyatin, “charge you with a charge”, a dying man's last request; the shadda of بوصيّة is printed. wa-huwa, masculine though waṣiyya is feminine: the pronoun points to the matter rather than the word. annī, “that I …”, opens a clause that is never finished: after idhā raʾaytanī muttu, “when you see me, I have died”, the speaker turns to a command, idhhab, “go”, and the imperative stands without the fa- that Classical Arabic puts at the head of such an answer. In raʾaytanī muttu the second verb says what is seen. akhbir, imperative of Form IV akhbara, “to inform”.

sentences.t: وَأَوْصِهَا أَنْ تَأْتِيَ إِلَى هَذَا الْمَكَانِ لِأَجْلِ أَنْ تَأْخُذَ عَزَائِي وَتَحْضُرَ غُسْلِي وَأَوْصِهَا أَنْ تَكُونَ صَابِرَةً عَلَى فِرَاقِي
sentences.tr: wa-awṣihā an taʾtiya ilā hādhā al-makāni li-ajli an taʾkhudha ʿazāʾī wa-taḥḍura ghuslī wa-awṣihā an takūna ṣābiratan ʿalā firāqī
sentences.l: and charge-her that she-come to this place for-the-sake-of that she-take my-condolence and attend my-washing; and charge-her that she-be patient over my-parting.”
sentences.i: and bid her come to this place to receive the condolences for me and be present at the washing of my body; and bid her bear my loss with patience.”
sentences.n: awṣi, imperative of awṣā, the defective verb losing its final vowel; an with the subjunctive gives what she is charged to do. akhadha al-ʿazāʾa, “to take the condolence”, to receive the visits of sympathy as the bereaved does; the hamza of عزائي is printed. ḥaḍara, “to be present at”. ghusl, the ritual washing of the dead before burial. ṣabara ʿalā, “to be patient under”; firāq, “parting”, here his death.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ خَرَّ مَغْشِيًّا عَلَيْهِ
sentences.tr: thumma kharra maghshiyyan ʿalayhi
sentences.l: Then he-fell, fainted upon-him.
sentences.i: Then he fell down in a faint.
sentences.n: kharra, “to fall down”; its shadda is printed. maghshiyyan ʿalayhi, “swooned upon”, passive participle of ghashiya with ʿalayhi, the fixed idiom for fainting, standing as a ḥāl.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا أَفَاقَ سَمِعَ جَارِيَةً تُغَنِّى مِنْ بَعِيدٍ وَتُنْشِدُ الْأَشْعَارَ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā afāqa samiʿa jāriyatan tughannī min baʿīdin wa-tunshidu al-ashʿāra
sentences.l: And when he-came-round, he-heard a-slave-girl singing from afar and reciting the poems.
sentences.i: When he came to himself he heard a slave-girl singing in the distance and reciting verses.
sentences.n: afāqa, Form IV, “to come round”. تغنّى is read tughannī, Form II imperfect of ghannā, “to sing”, with the final ي printed as ى, as often in this edition; the shadda is printed. taghannā, Form V perfect, “she sang”, is also possible, but the imperfect matches tunshidu beside it. A verb after an indefinite noun describes it: jāriyatan tughannī, “a girl singing”. anshada, Form IV, “to recite (verse)”.

sentences.t: فَصَارَ يُصْغِي إِلَيْهَا وَيَسْمَعُ صَوْتَهَا وَهُوَ تَارَةً يَسْكَرُ وَتَارَةً يَصْحُو وَتَارَةً يَبْكِي شَجَنًا وَحُزْنًا مِمَّا أَصَابَهُ
sentences.tr: fa-ṣāra yuṣghī ilayhā wa-yasmaʿu ṣawtahā wa-huwa tāratan yaskaru wa-tāratan yaṣḥū wa-tāratan yabkī shajanan wa-ḥuznan mimmā aṣābahu
sentences.l: And he-fell-to listening to-her and hearing her-voice, and he (was) one-time getting-drunk, and one-time coming-sober, and one-time weeping, (from) grief and sorrow, at-what had-befallen-him.
sentences.i: He lay listening to her, hearing her voice; and now he was as if drunk, now sober again, and now he wept for grief and sorrow at what had befallen him.
sentences.n: ṣāra with the imperfect, “to fall to (doing)”. aṣghā ilā, Form IV, “to bend the ear to”. tāratan … tāratan, “at one time … at another”. sakira, “to be drunk”, here with love and song; ṣaḥā, “to sober up”. shajanan wa-ḥuznan, accusatives of cause, “out of grief and sorrow”. mimmā = min mā, “at what”.

sentences.t: فَسَمِعَ الْجَارِيَةَ الَّتِي تُغَنِّى تُنْشِدُ هَذِهِ الْأَبْيَاتَ
sentences.tr: fa-samiʿa al-jāriyata allatī tughannī tunshidu hādhihi al-abyāta
sentences.l: And he-heard the slave-girl who sings reciting these lines:
sentences.i: And he heard the singing girl recite these lines:
sentences.n: allatī tughannī, “who was singing”, again with ى printed for final ي. tunshidu, a second verb saying what he heard her do. abyāt, plural of bayt, a line of verse.

sentences.t:
عَجَّلَ الْبَيْنُ بَيْنَنَا بِالْفِرَاقِ * بَعْدَ اِلْفِ وَجِيْرَة وَاتِّفَاقِ
فَرَّقَتْ بَيْنَنَا صُرُوفُ اللَّيَالِيْ * لَيْتَ شِعْرِي مَتَى يَكُونُ التَّلَاقِيْ
مَا اَمَرَّ الْفِرَاقَ بَعْدَ اجْتِمَاعِ * لَيْتَهُ مَا اَضَرَّ بِالْعُشَّاقِ
غُصَّةُ الْمَوْتِ سَاعَةٌ ثُمَّ تَقْضِيْ * وَفِرَاقُ الْحَبِيْبِ فِى الْقَلْبِ بَاقِيْ
لَوْ وَجَدْنَا اِلَى الْفِرَاقِ سَبِيْلًا * لَاَذَقْنَا الْفِرَاقَ طَعْمَ الْفِرَاقِ
sentences.tr:
ʿajjala al-baynu baynanā bi-al-firāqi * baʿda ilfin wa-jīratin wa-ittifāqi
farraqat baynanā ṣurūfu al-layālī * layta shiʿrī matā yakūnu al-talāqī
mā amarra al-firāqa baʿda ijtimāʿin * laytahu mā aḍarra bi-al-ʿushshāqi
ghuṣṣatu al-mawti sāʿatun thumma taqḍī * wa-firāqu al-ḥabībi fī al-qalbi bāqī
law wajadnā ilā al-firāqi sabīlan * la-adhaqnā al-firāqa ṭaʿma al-firāqi
sentences.l:
Severance hastened, between-us, the separation, * after familiarity and neighbourliness and accord.
The turns of the nights have-divided between-us; * would-that (were) my-knowing: when will-be the meeting-again?
How bitter (is) the separation after coming-together! * Would-that-it did not harm the lovers.
The choking of death (is) an-hour, then it-is-done; * and the separation of the beloved in the heart (is) remaining.
If we-found to the separation a-way, * we-would-make-taste the separation the taste of the separation.
sentences.i:
Parting has come too soon between us and severed us, after the friendship of neighbours living in one accord.
The turns of the nights have divided us: would that I knew when we shall meet again!
How bitter is parting, after being together! Would that it did no harm to lovers!
The pang of death lasts an hour and then is over; but parting from the beloved stays in the heart.
If we could only find a way to get at parting itself, we would make parting taste what parting tastes like.
sentences.n: Metre: khafīf, rhyming in -āqi. The pointing is the print's own and is kept as printed, including the bare alif of اِلْف, اَمَرَّ, اَضَرَّ, اِلَى and لَاَذَقْنَا, where the edition marks no hamza. al-bayn, “severance”, chimes with baynanā, “between us”, and the jingle comes back in the second line; ʿajjala … bi-al-firāqi, “hastened the separation”, the verb taking its object with bi-. ilf, “familiarity”. وَجِيْرَة is printed with no final vowel; the metre wants jīratin, “neighbourliness”. ṣurūf al-layālī, “the turns of the nights”, the shifts of fortune. layta shiʿrī, “would that my knowing (were)”, the stock “I wish I knew”. mā amarra, “how bitter”, the pattern of wonder mā afʿala, with al-firāqa its object. اِلْفِ and اجْتِمَاعِ each carry a single kasra in the print, though grammar and metre want ilfin and ijtimāʿin; the transliteration gives the full forms, as it gives jīratin. aḍarra bi-, Form IV, “to harm”: the verb chooses bi- for the one harmed. ghuṣṣa, “a choking in the throat”, the agony of dying; taqḍī, “it ends”, from qaḍā in its sense “to be finished”. In the last line la- opens the answer to law; adhāqa, Form IV, “to make taste”, takes two objects, al-firāqa and ṭaʿma al-firāqi: if parting could be caught, the lovers would give it a dose of its own bitterness.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعَ ابْنُ بَكَّارٍ إِنْشَادَ الْجَارِيَةِ شَهَقَ شَهْقَةً فَارَقَتْ رُوحُهُ جَسَدَهُ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿa ibnu Bakkārin inshāda al-jāriyati shahaqa shahqatan fāraqat rūḥuhu jasadahu
sentences.l: And when Ibn Bakkār heard the reciting of the slave-girl, he-gasped a-gasp, his-soul parted his-body.
sentences.i: When Ibn Bakkār heard the girl's song, he gave one sobbing gasp, and his soul left his body.
sentences.n: inshād, verbal noun of anshada, “reciting, chanting”. shahaqa shahqatan, “he gasped a gasp”, the verb with its own verbal noun: a single deep sob. fāraqat rūḥuhu jasadahu, “his soul parted (from) his body”, can be read as describing the gasp, “a gasp with which his soul left him”, or as a fresh statement. rūḥ, “soul”, is treated as feminine here (fāraqat).

sentences.t: قَالَ الْجَوْهَرِيُّ فَلَمَّا رَأَيْتُهُ مَاتَ أَوْصَيْتُ عَلَيْهِ صَاحِبَ الدَّارِ وَقُلْتُ لَهُ اعْلَمْ أَنَّنِي ذَاهِبٌ إِلَى بَغْدَادَ لِأُخْبِرَ أَهْلَهُ وَأَقَارِبَهُ حَتَّى يَأْتُوا لِيُجَهِّزُوهُ
sentences.tr: qāla al-jawhariyyu fa-lammā raʾaytuhu māta awṣaytu ʿalayhi ṣāḥiba al-dāri wa-qultu lahu iʿlam annanī dhāhibun ilā Baghdāda li-ukhbira ahlahu wa-aqāribahu ḥattā yaʾtū li-yujahhizūhu
sentences.l: The jeweller said: And when I-saw-him (that) he-had-died, I-charged concerning-him the owner of the house, and I-said to-him: Know that-I (am) going to Baghdad to-inform his-family and his-kinsmen, so-that they-come to-make-him-ready.
sentences.i: The jeweller said: When I saw that he was dead, I left him in the care of the master of the house and said to him, “I am going to Baghdad to tell his family and his kin, so that they may come and prepare him for burial.”
sentences.n: The print has رأبته, a misprint for رأيته, corrected here. raʾaytuhu māta, “I saw him, he had died”, as with raʾaytanī muttu above. awṣā ʿalā, “to commend (someone) to another's care”: ʿalayhi is the dead man, ṣāḥiba al-dāri the one charged. li-ukhbira, li- “in order to” with the subjunctive. aqārib, “relatives”. jahhaza, Form II, “to equip”, of the dead “to prepare for burial”, washing and shrouding; li- again “in order to”. Baghdād is diptote.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنِّي أَتَيْتُ إِلَى بَغْدَادَ وَدَخَلْتُ دَارِي وَغَيَّرْتُ ثِيَابِي وَبَعْدَ ذَلِكَ جِئْتُ إِلَى دَارِ عَلِيِّ بْنِ بَكَّارٍ
sentences.tr: thumma innī ataytu ilā Baghdāda wa-dakhaltu dārī wa-ghayyartu thiyābī wa-baʿda dhālika jiʾtu ilā dāri ʿAliyyi ibni Bakkārin
sentences.l: Then (indeed) I came to Baghdad, and entered my-house, and changed my-clothes, and after that I-came to the house of ʿAlī ibn Bakkār.
sentences.i: Then I came to Baghdad, went into my house and changed my clothes, and after that I went to ʿAlī ibn Bakkār's house.
sentences.n: atā ilā, “to come to”: Classical atā takes its goal directly. ghayyara, Form II, “to change”. jiʾtu, “I came”, from jāʾa; the hamza of جئت is printed.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا رَآنِي غِلْمَانُهُ أَتَوْا إِلَيَّ وَسَأَلُونِي عَنْهُ وَسَأَلْتُهُمْ أَنْ يَسْتَأْذِنُوا لِي بِالدُّخُولِ عَلَى وَالِدَتِهِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā raʾānī ghilmānuhu ataw ilayya wa-saʾalūnī ʿanhu wa-saʾaltuhum an yastaʾdhinū lī bi-al-dukhūli ʿalā wālidatihi
sentences.l: And when his-pages saw-me, they-came to-me and asked-me about-him; and I-asked-them that they-seek-leave for-me for the entering upon his-mother.
sentences.i: When his pages saw me they came up to me and asked after him, and I asked them to seek leave for me to go in to his mother.
sentences.n: raʾānī, a singular verb before its plural subject ghilmān, as Classical Arabic allows; its madda is printed. ghilmān, plural of ghulām, “page, young servant”. The shadda of اليّ is printed. istaʾdhana, Form X of adhina, “to ask leave”: li- marks the one on whose behalf, bi- the thing asked for; al-dukhūl ʿalā, “going in to (someone)”.

sentences.t: فَأَذِنَتْ لِي بِالدُّخُولِ فَدَخَلْتُ وَسَلَّمْتُ عَلَيْهَا
sentences.tr: fa-adhinat lī bi-al-dukhūli fa-dakhaltu wa-sallamtu ʿalayhā
sentences.l: And she-permitted me (for) the entering, and I-entered and gave-greeting to-her.
sentences.i: She gave me leave to come in; I went in and greeted her.
sentences.n: adhina li- … bi-, “to give (someone) leave for (something)”: li- marks the one permitted, bi- what is allowed. sallama ʿalā, Form II, “to greet (someone) with salām”.

sentences.t: وَقُلْتُ إِنَّ اللَّهَ مُدَبِّرُ الْأَنْفَاسِ بِأَمْرِهِ وَإِذَا قَضَى أَمْرًا لَا مَفَرَّ مِنْ قَضَائِهِ وَمَاكَانَ لِنَفْسٍ أَنْ تَمُوتَ إِلَّا بِإِذْنِ اللَّهِ كِتَابًا مُؤَجَّلًا
sentences.tr: wa-qultu inna Allāha mudabbiru al-anfāsi bi-amrihi wa-idhā qaḍā amran lā mafarra min qaḍāʾihi wa-mā kāna li-nafsin an tamūta illā bi-idhni Allāhi kitāban muʾajjalan
sentences.l: And I-said: (Indeed) God (is) the disposer of the breaths by His-command, and when He-decrees a-matter, no fleeing from His-decree; and it-was not for a-soul that it-die except by the leave of God, a-writ term-appointed.
sentences.i: And I said, “God orders every breath we draw by His command, and when He decrees a thing there is no escaping His decree: no soul may die except by God's leave, at a term written and fixed.”
sentences.n: mudabbir, Form II participle of dabbara, “to order, govern”; al-anfās, “the breaths”, each life counted out breath by breath. In idhā qaḍā amran the answer lā mafarra stands without fa-, as often in this text; mafarr, “a place to flee to”, with lā of absolute negation. The last clause is Qurʾān 3:145 and is vocalised in its Qurʾānic pointing; the print runs ماكان together, and the fatḥa of تموتَ and the shadda of مؤجّلا are printed. mā kāna li-…an, “it was not for … to”, it is not possible. kitāban muʾajjalan, “(by) a writ with a fixed term”, accusative: the hour of death is written down and appointed. The jeweller breaks the news by way of these commonplaces of resignation, without saying it outright.

sentences.t: فَتَوَهَّمَتْ أُمُّ عَلِيِّ بْنِ بَكَّارٍ مِنْ هَذَا الْكَلَامِ أَنَّ ابْنَهَا قَدْمَاتَ فَبَكَتْ بُكَاءً شَدِيدًا
sentences.tr: fa-tawahhamat ummu ʿAliyyi ibni Bakkārin min hādhā al-kalāmi anna ibnahā qad māta fa-bakat bukāʾan shadīdan
sentences.l: And the mother of ʿAlī ibn Bakkār supposed from this speech that her-son had-died, and she-wept a-weeping vehement.
sentences.i: From these words ʿAlī ibn Bakkār's mother guessed that her son was dead, and she wept bitterly.
sentences.n: tawahhama, Form V, “to suppose, suspect”. قدمات is printed as one word: qad māta, “has died”. bakat bukāʾan shadīdan, the verb with its own verbal noun and an adjective, “wept a vehement weeping”.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ قَالَتْ بِاللَّهِ عَلَيْكَ أَنْ تُخْبِرَنِي هَلْ تُوُفِّيَ وَلَدِى
sentences.tr: thumma qālat bi-Allāhi ʿalayka an tukhbiranī hal tuwuffiya waladī
sentences.l: Then she-said: By God (I adjure) upon-you, that you-tell-me: has my-son been-taken (in death)?
sentences.i: Then she said, “By God, I beg you, tell me: has my son died?”
sentences.n: bi-Allāhi ʿalayka, “by God, (I lay it) on you”: bi- is the bi- of oath, and ʿalayka marks the one adjured. an tukhbiranī, “that you tell me”, gives the thing begged for, a loose construction; Classical Arabic would rather say illā mā akhbartanī. tuwuffiya, passive of tawaffā, “to be taken (by God)”, to die. ولدى is printed with ى.

sentences.t: فَلَمْ أَقْدِرْأَنْ أَرُدَّ عَلَيْهَا جَوَابًا مِنَ الْبُكَاءِ وَكَثْرَةِ الْجَزَعِ
sentences.tr: fa-lam aqdir an arudda ʿalayhā jawāban mina al-bukāʾi wa-kathrati al-jazaʿi
sentences.l: And I-could not that I-return to-her an-answer, from the weeping and the abundance of the anguish.
sentences.i: But I could not give her any answer for weeping and the depth of my grief.
sentences.n: اقدران is printed as one word: aqdir an. qadara, “to be able”, jussive after lam. radda ʿalā … jawāban, “to return an answer to”. min, “from, because of”. jazaʿ, “anguish, loss of composure”.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا رَأَتْنِي عَلَى تِلْكَ الْحَالَةِ انْخَنَقَتْ بِالْبُكَاءِ ثُمَّ وَقَعَتْ عَلَى الْأَرْضِ مَغْشِيًّا عَلَيْهَا
sentences.tr: fa-lammā raʾatnī ʿalā tilka al-ḥālati inkhanaqat bi-al-bukāʾi thumma waqaʿat ʿalā al-arḍi maghshiyyan ʿalayhā
sentences.l: And when she-saw-me in that state, she-choked with the weeping, then fell on the ground, fainted upon-her.
sentences.i: When she saw me in that state she choked with sobs, and then fell to the ground in a faint.
sentences.n: The print has رأنني, a misprint for رأتني, corrected here. ʿalā tilka al-ḥālati, “in that state”. inkhanaqa, Form VII of khanaqa, “to be choked”; bi- marks the cause, “with weeping”. maghshiyyan ʿalayhā, the fainting idiom again, the pronoun now feminine.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا أَفَاقَتْ مِنْ غَشْيَتِهَا قَالَتْ مَا كَانَ مِنْ أَمْرِ وَلَدِى
sentences.tr: fa-lammā afāqat min ghashyatihā qālat mā kāna min amri waladī
sentences.l: And when she-came-round from her-swoon, she-said: What was of the affair of my-son?
sentences.i: When she came out of her faint she said, “What has happened to my son?”
sentences.n: ghashya, “a swoon”. mā kāna min amri …, “what there was of the affair of …”, the stock way of asking what happened to someone.

sentences.t: فَقُلْتُ لَهَا أَعْظَمَ اللَّهُ أَجْرَكِ فِيهِ
sentences.tr: fa-qultu lahā aʿẓama Allāhu ajraki fīhi
sentences.l: And I-said to-her: May God make-great your-reward in-him.
sentences.i: I said to her, “May God make great your reward for your loss of him.”
sentences.n: aʿẓama Allāhu ajraki, “may God make your reward great”, the perfect used as a wish: the formula of condolence on a death, promising the bereaved God's reward for patience under the loss. The kasra of اجركِ, marking a woman addressed, is printed.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنِّي حَدَّثْتُهَا بِمَا كَانَ مِنْ أَمْرِهِ مِنَ الِابْتِدَاءِ إِلَى الِانْتِهَاءِ
sentences.tr: thumma innī ḥaddathtuhā bi-mā kāna min amrihi mina al-ibtidāʾi ilā al-intihāʾi
sentences.l: Then (indeed) I told-her of-what was of his-affair, from the beginning to the ending.
sentences.i: Then I told her all that had happened to him, from beginning to end.
sentences.n: ḥaddatha bi-, Form II, “to tell (someone) of”: bi- marks what is told. ibtidāʾ and intihāʾ, Form VIII verbal nouns, “beginning” and “ending”, a rhyming pair.

sentences.t: فَقَالَتْ هَلْ أَوْصَاكَ بِشَيْءٍ
sentences.tr: fa-qālat hal awṣāka bi-shayʾin
sentences.l: And she-said: Did he-charge-you with a-thing?
sentences.i: She said, “Did he leave any charge with you?”
sentences.n: awṣā bi-, “to charge (someone) with”: the verb chooses bi- for the thing enjoined. The hamza of بشيء is printed.

sentences.t: فَقُلْتُ لَهَا نَعَمْ وَحَكَيْتُ لَهَا عَلَى مَا أَوْصَانِي بِهِ
sentences.tr: fa-qultu lahā naʿam wa-ḥakaytu lahā ʿalā mā awṣānī bihi
sentences.l: And I-said to-her: Yes; and I-related to-her about what he-charged-me with-it.
sentences.i: I told her yes, and related to her what he had charged me with.
sentences.n: ḥakā li- … ʿalā, “to relate to (someone) about”: Classical ḥakā takes the thing told as a direct object, and the ʿalā is a later, colloquial usage. mā awṣānī bihi, “what he charged me with”, bihi taking up mā.

sentences.t: وَقُلْتُ لَهَا أَسْرِعِي فِي تَجْهِيزِهِ
sentences.tr: wa-qultu lahā asriʿī fī tajhīzihi
sentences.l: And I-said to-her: Hasten in his-preparing.
sentences.i: And I said to her, “Make haste to prepare him for burial.”
sentences.n: asriʿī, feminine imperative of Form IV asraʿa, “to hasten”. tajhīz, verbal noun of jahhaza, the laying-out of the dead.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعَتْ أُمُّ عَلِيِّ بْنِ بَكَّارٍ كَلَامِي سَقَطَتْ مَغْشِيًّا عَلَيْهَا
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿat ummu ʿAliyyi ibni Bakkārin kalāmī saqaṭat maghshiyyan ʿalayhā
sentences.l: And when the mother of ʿAlī ibn Bakkār heard my-speech, she-fell, fainted upon-her.
sentences.i: When ʿAlī ibn Bakkār's mother heard what I said, she fell down in a faint.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا أَفَاقَتْ عَزَمَتْ عَلَى مَا أَوْصَيْتُهَا بِهِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā afāqat ʿazamat ʿalā mā awṣaytuhā bihi
sentences.l: And when she-came-round, she-resolved on what I-had-charged-her with-it.
sentences.i: When she came round, she set about doing what I had told her.
sentences.n: ʿazama ʿalā, “to resolve on, set about”. The jeweller says awṣaytuhā, “I charged her”: he passes on ʿAlī's charge as his own.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنِّي ذَهَبْتُ إِلَى دَارِي وَصِرْتُ فِى الطَّرِيقِ أَتَفَكَّرُ فِى حُسْنِ شَبَابِهِ
sentences.tr: thumma innī dhahabtu ilā dārī wa-ṣirtu fī al-ṭarīqi atafakkaru fī ḥusni shabābihi
sentences.l: Then (indeed) I went to my-house, and I-fell-to, on the road, thinking on the beauty of his-youth.
sentences.i: Then I went off home, and all along the road I kept thinking of his youth and his good looks.
sentences.n: The shadda of انّي is printed, and فى is printed with ى. ṣāra with the imperfect, “to fall to (doing)”. tafakkara fī, Form V, “to reflect on”. ḥusnu shabābihi, “the beauty of his youth”.

sentences.t: فَبَيْنَمَا أَنَا كَذَلِكَ وَإِذَا بِامْرَأَةٍ قَدْ قَبَضَتْ عَلَي يَدِي
sentences.tr: fa-baynamā anā ka-dhālika wa-idhā bi-imraʾatin qad qabaḍat ʿalā yadī
sentences.l: And while I (was) like that, and behold, a-woman had seized on my-hand.
sentences.i: And while I was in this state, a woman suddenly caught hold of my hand.
sentences.n: baynamā …, “while …”, its main clause opened by wa-idhā, “and behold”; after idhā of surprise bi- only marks what appears. The hamza of بامرأة is printed. qabaḍa ʿalā, “to take hold of”. علي is the print's spelling of ʿalā, with ي. The night breaks off on this moment of suspense.

sentences.t: وَأَدْرَكَ شَهْرَزَادَ الصَّبَاحُ فَسَكَتَتْ عَنِ الْكَلَامِ الْمُبَاحِ
sentences.tr: wa-adraka Shahrazāda al-ṣabāḥu fa-sakatat ʿani al-kalāmi al-mubāḥi
sentences.l: And the morning overtook Shahrazād, and she-fell-silent from the permitted speech.
sentences.i: And morning overtook Shahrazād, and she fell silent from the speech allowed her.
sentences.n: The object comes before the subject: Shahrazāda is the one overtaken, al-ṣabāḥu the morning that overtakes. al-kalām al-mubāḥ, “the permitted speech”; the rhyme ṣabāḥ / mubāḥ closes every night.
